title: Feminist organisations call march against gender violence in Lyon

tea.why: Protesters are marching to oppose gender-based, social, and state violence following the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.
tea.want: The organisers are demanding that the state allocate 3 billion euros to combat sexist and sexual violence.
tea.changed: Nov 26: The prefecture of the Rhone confirmed the march is scheduled to depart from Place Bellecour at 15:00.

summary: Feminist organisations, including NousToutes Rhone, have scheduled a march in Lyon for Saturday, November 28, to protest against gender-based, social, and state violence. The demonstration is set to begin at 15:00 at Place Bellecour and conclude at Place Jean-Mace. The organisers are calling for the state to provide 3 billion euros to address sexist and sexual violence. Additionally, the Coordination nationale des Gilets jaunes has announced its participation, designating the event as its seventh act of protest. While the prefecture of the Rhone has officially acknowledged the feminist march, it has not commented on other gatherings associated with the Gilets jaunes. The event follows previous restrictions on protests in the city centre imposed by the prefecture following incidents in October.
demands: Allocate 3 billion euros to combat sexist and sexual violence
response: The prefecture of the Rhone has officially acknowledged the march organised by feminist associations.

updates.text: The prefecture of the Rhone confirmed the march is scheduled to depart from Place Bellecour at 15:00.
